difficultyReason: The stimulus uses a disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B). Distractors share topical surface features or use valid but structurally different forms (e.g., modus ponens, contrapositive). Students must formalize the argument to avoid being misled by subject-matter overlap.
stimulus: Either the medication caused the patient's rash or the rash resulted from an allergic reaction to a food. The patient has not eaten any allergenic foods in the past week. Therefore, the medication caused the rash.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Either the defendant committed the fraud alone or had an accomplice. Investigators found no evidence of an accomplice. Therefore, the defendant committed the fraud alone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the bridge collapses, either faulty materials or poor design is to blame. The design was certified as sound. Therefore, faulty materials caused the collapse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The patient's rash is severe. All severe rashes require immediate treatment. Therefore, the patient's rash requires immediate treatment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If the medication is discontinued, the rash will clear up. The rash has not cleared up. Therefore, the medication has not been discontinued.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The patient could have developed the rash from either medication or stress. Both the medication and a stressful event occurred last week. Therefore, it is unclear which caused the rash.

explanations.correct: Both the stimulus and choice A follow disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not B; therefore A. The stimulus eliminates food allergy and concludes medication; choice A eliminates the accomplice and concludes the defendant acted alone. Structure matches perfectly.
explanations.A: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism: (fraud alone) or (had accomplice); no accomplice; therefore fraud alone. Identical logical form to the stimulus.
explanations.B: Same topic area (causes and elimination) but adds a conditional premise ('If the bridge collapses…'), making it a conditional chain with elimination rather than a pure disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.C: This is a universal-to-particular inference (All severe rashes → treatment; this rash is severe; therefore treatment). Different logical form from the stimulus's disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.D: This is modus tollens: If medication discontinued → rash clears; rash has not cleared; therefore medication not discontinued. Different logical form, even though the subject matter resembles the stimulus.
explanations.E: The argument does not eliminate either disjunct and instead withholds a conclusion. This is not a disjunctive syllogism and does not parallel the stimulus.

difficultyReason: The stimulus is a conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A; therefore C). Distractors include a contrapositive, a topic-matching invalid form, and a universal-to-particular instantiation. Students who only recognize the conclusion may select the topic-similar wrong answer.
stimulus: Whenever a government imposes price controls, shortages eventually develop. Whenever shortages develop, black markets emerge. The current government has imposed price controls. Therefore, black markets will eventually emerge.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a forest fire goes uncontrolled, it depletes soil nutrients. Depleted soil nutrients prevent forest regrowth. A fire in the northern district is uncontrolled. Therefore, forest regrowth in the northern district will be prevented.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Price controls distort market signals. Distorted market signals are undesirable. Therefore, price controls should be abolished.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever inflation rises, central banks raise interest rates. Interest rates have not been raised. Therefore, inflation has not risen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All economies that impose price controls eventually transition to free markets. Country X has imposed price controls. Therefore, Country X will eventually transition to a free market.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some governments that impose price controls succeed in stabilizing prices. This government has imposed price controls. Therefore, this government may succeed in stabilizing prices.

explanations.correct: Both the stimulus and choice A employ a conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A is true; therefore C). Stimulus: price controls → shortages → black markets; controls imposed; therefore black markets emerge. Choice A: fire uncontrolled → soil depleted → regrowth prevented; fire is uncontrolled; therefore regrowth prevented.
explanations.A: Correct. Three-step conditional chain with affirmation of the antecedent. Matches the stimulus's structure exactly.
explanations.B: Only two premises, no instantiated case. The conclusion ('should be abolished') introduces a normative element absent from the stimulus. Different form.
explanations.C: This is modus tollens applied to a conditional (if inflation rises → rates rise; rates not raised; therefore inflation not risen). The stimulus affirms the antecedent; this denies the consequent.
explanations.D: This is a universal-to-particular instantiation (All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B) with only two inferential steps, not a three-link chain. Missing the middle conditional step.
explanations.E: Uses 'some' rather than 'whenever/all,' weakening the premise. The conclusion ('may succeed') is weaker than the stimulus's definite conclusion. Strength mismatch.

difficultyReason: The stimulus uses modus tollens (A → B; not B; therefore not A). Distractors include a disjunctive syllogism with the same subject domain, a modus ponens, and a same-topic invalid argument. Students who recognize 'if–then' structure but not direction of inference may pick the modus ponens trap.
stimulus: If the archaeological site is more than 3,000 years old, the pottery fragments found there will exhibit a particular type of oxidation pattern. The pottery fragments do not exhibit that oxidation pattern. Therefore, the site is not more than 3,000 years old.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a star is in the main sequence, its core temperature exceeds ten million degrees. This star's core temperature does not exceed ten million degrees. Therefore, this star is not in the main sequence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the pottery fragments are ancient, they are fragile. These pottery fragments are ancient. Therefore, these pottery fragments are fragile.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the site is Bronze Age or it is Iron Age. The site is not Iron Age. Therefore, the site is Bronze Age.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most ancient sites contain pottery. This site contains pottery. Therefore, this site is probably ancient.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the site lacks an oxidation pattern, it is less than 3,000 years old. The site lacks the oxidation pattern. Therefore, the site is less than 3,000 years old.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is modus tollens: If P → Q; not Q; therefore not P. Choice A matches exactly: if main sequence → core temp > 10M; core temp not > 10M; therefore not main sequence.
explanations.A: Correct. Modus tollens with identical two-premise structure and denial of the consequent leading to denial of the antecedent.
explanations.B: This is modus ponens (If P → Q; P; therefore Q), the opposite inferential direction from the stimulus. Surface similarity to the stimulus's subject matter is a trap.
explanations.C: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not B; therefore A). Valid, but a different logical form from the stimulus's modus tollens.
explanations.D: Reversed base-rate reasoning ('most A have B; x has B; therefore x is probably A'). This is a flawed argument and does not match the valid modus tollens of the stimulus.
explanations.E: Though it reaches a similar conclusion, this is modus ponens (If lacks pattern → < 3,000 years; lacks pattern; therefore < 3,000 years). The conditional is constructed differently — the absence of the pattern is directly stated as the antecedent, not derived.

difficultyReason: The stimulus uses universal instantiation (All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B). One distractor uses 'most' instead of 'all,' creating a strength-shift trap. Another uses the same subject but reverses the universal claim. Students must track quantifier strength carefully.
stimulus: All legislative bills that pass without a supermajority are subject to gubernatorial veto. The education reform bill passed without a supermajority. Therefore, the education reform bill is subject to gubernatorial veto.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every chemical compound that contains chlorine is potentially hazardous to marine life. This new industrial solvent contains chlorine. Therefore, this solvent is potentially hazardous to marine life.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most bills that bypass committee review are subject to floor amendments. This bill bypassed committee review. Therefore, this bill is probably subject to floor amendments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The education reform bill was hastily drafted. Hastily drafted bills often contain errors. Therefore, the education reform bill likely contains errors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a bill is vetoed, the legislature can override the veto with a two-thirds majority. The legislature does not have a two-thirds majority. Therefore, any vetoed bill will stand.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No bill lacking bipartisan support has ever been enacted without controversy. This bill lacks bipartisan support. Therefore, if enacted, this bill will be controversial.

explanations.correct: Both the stimulus and choice A use universal instantiation: All/every A are B; x is A; therefore x is B. The universal claim is categorical ('all'/'every'), the particular is identified, and the conclusion is certain. Structure matches perfectly.
explanations.A: Correct. Every chlorine-containing compound is hazardous; this solvent contains chlorine; therefore it is hazardous. Same universal-to-particular form with matching conclusion strength.
explanations.B: Uses 'most' instead of 'all,' weakening the universal premise, and 'probably' in the conclusion. Strength-shift trap — the conclusion's certainty does not match the stimulus.
explanations.C: Uses 'often' (not 'all'), and 'likely' in the conclusion. Same strength-shift trap as B. Also matches topic (legislative bills) to lure students away from structural analysis.
explanations.D: This is modus tollens (if veto → can override; cannot override; therefore veto stands). Different logical form, though it uses legislative vocabulary.
explanations.E: Contains a conditional conclusion ('if enacted, will be controversial'), which is not a simple categorical conclusion. The stimulus concludes categorically, not conditionally.

difficultyReason: The stimulus uses a contrapositive derivation embedded in an argument: a conditional plus its contrapositive application. Distractors use modus ponens with the same antecedent-consequent vocabulary, which tempts students who misread the direction of the inference.
stimulus: A language will retain its native speaker base only if younger generations continue to acquire it as a first language. Younger generations in this community have stopped acquiring the language as a first language. Therefore, this language will not retain its native speaker base.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A theater company survives only if it attracts new audiences each season. This theater company has not attracted new audiences this season. Therefore, this theater company will not survive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a language loses its native speaker base, it becomes a dead language. This language has lost its native speaker base. Therefore, this language will become a dead language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever younger generations stop learning a language, cultural traditions tied to it disappear. Younger generations have stopped learning this language. Therefore, the cultural traditions tied to it will disappear.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A language retains its speakers only if it is taught in schools. This language is taught in schools. Therefore, this language will retain its speakers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Either a language is supported by government policy or it gradually disappears. This language is not supported by government policy. Therefore, it will gradually disappear.

explanations.correct: The stimulus uses 'only if,' which means: retains base → younger generations acquire it. The second premise denies the consequent (younger generations have NOT acquired it), yielding modus tollens: not consequent, therefore not antecedent (will not retain base). Choice A has identical structure: survives → attracts new audiences; has NOT attracted new audiences; therefore will not survive.
explanations.A: Correct. 'Only if' conditional plus denial of the consequent (modus tollens). Structure is identical to the stimulus.
explanations.B: This is modus ponens (if loses base → dead language; has lost base; therefore dead language). Different direction of inference. The 'only if' structure is absent.
explanations.C: This is a standard conditional chain affirming the antecedent (modus ponens with 'whenever'). No 'only if' construction; the direction of inference differs from the stimulus.
explanations.D: This commits the fallacy of affirming the consequent (retains speakers → taught in schools; taught in schools; therefore retains speakers). This is invalid reasoning, whereas the stimulus is valid.
explanations.E: Disjunctive syllogism structure (A or B; not A; therefore B). Valid, but a different logical form from the stimulus's modus tollens via 'only if.'

difficultyReason: The stimulus uses a two-premise analogy structure (X is like Y in relevant ways; Y has property R; therefore X has property R). Distractors include a universal instantiation that superficially resembles an analogy, and a topic-similar choice with an additional unsupported premise.
stimulus: Crowdfunding platforms operate in the same regulatory environment and serve the same investor base as traditional securities exchanges. Traditional securities exchanges are required to disclose all material risks to investors. Therefore, crowdfunding platforms should also be required to disclose all material risks to investors.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community-supported agriculture programs operate under the same food safety standards and serve the same consumers as licensed grocery stores. Licensed grocery stores must display nutritional information on all products. Therefore, community-supported agriculture programs should also display nutritional information.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All financial institutions that accept deposits from the public must carry deposit insurance. Crowdfunding platforms accept deposits from the public. Therefore, crowdfunding platforms must carry deposit insurance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Securities exchanges and crowdfunding platforms are both profit-driven. Profit-driven institutions sometimes prioritize revenue over investor protection. Therefore, crowdfunding platforms may sometimes prioritize revenue over investor protection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Traditional securities exchanges were once unregulated and experienced frequent fraud. Since crowdfunding platforms are currently unregulated, they will also experience frequent fraud.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Crowdfunding platforms raise capital from the public, as do municipal bond issuers. Municipal bond issuers are subject to audit requirements. The public deserves protection. Therefore, crowdfunding platforms should be subject to audit requirements.

explanations.correct: The stimulus argues by analogy: X and Y share the same regulatory environment and investor base (relevant similarities); Y has requirement R; therefore X should have R. Choice A mirrors this exactly: CSA programs and grocery stores share the same food safety standards and consumer base; grocery stores must display nutritional info; therefore CSA programs should too.
explanations.A: Correct. Two stated relevant similarities followed by a parallel obligation. Matches the analogy structure of the stimulus in both form and premise count.
explanations.B: This is universal instantiation (all A must carry insurance; crowdfunding platforms are A; therefore they must carry insurance). No analogy is drawn; the argument proceeds from a universal rule directly applied to a particular.
explanations.C: Shares only one similarity ('profit-driven'), not two. More importantly, the conclusion is weakened to 'may sometimes,' whereas the stimulus concludes with a definite normative obligation. Strength mismatch and structural shortfall.
explanations.D: This reasons from historical precedent to a causal prediction, not from shared characteristics to a shared obligation. Different argument form; also potentially invalid (post hoc).
explanations.E: Introduces an additional unsupported premise ('the public deserves protection') that the stimulus does not have. Three-premise structure does not match the stimulus's two-premise analogy.

difficultyReason: The stimulus is a disjunctive syllogism where the disjunction is presented as an exhaustive 'either…or.' One distractor uses a non-exhaustive 'either…or' that invalidates the inference; another uses the same subject matter but adds an unneeded premise. Students must check exhaustiveness.
stimulus: The sculpture was created either during the artist's early period or during the late period. Experts have conclusively established that it was not created during the late period. Therefore, the sculpture was created during the artist's early period.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The treaty was negotiated either under the current administration or the previous one. Historians have conclusively shown it was not negotiated under the current administration. Therefore, it was negotiated under the previous administration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The policy was introduced either to reduce crime or to increase tax revenue. It has not reduced crime. Therefore, it must have been introduced to increase tax revenue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sculpture may have been created during the early period. If created in the early period, it would exhibit rough textures. The sculpture has rough textures. Therefore, it was likely created during the early period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The composer wrote the symphony either in Vienna or Prague. The symphony was written in Vienna. Therefore, it was not written in Prague.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The painting was created in either the Renaissance or the Baroque period. Baroque characteristics are present. Therefore, the painting was created in the Baroque period.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a clean disjunctive syllogism: A or B (exhaustive); not B; therefore A. Choice A mirrors this exactly: treaty under current or previous administration; not current; therefore previous. Two-premise structure, eliminates one disjunct, concludes the other.
explanations.A: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism with the same two-premise structure. The disjunction is exhaustive (only two possible administrations), and one is eliminated, so the other must be true.
explanations.B: The disjunction ('to reduce crime or to increase revenue') is a stated purpose, not necessarily exhaustive — the policy could have been introduced for both reasons or neither. The elimination of one purpose does not conclusively establish the other. Structurally parallel in surface form but the exhaustiveness condition is weaker.
explanations.C: Uses probabilistic reasoning ('may have been,' 'likely') and affirms the consequent (if early → rough textures; has rough textures; therefore early). Different form and invalid structure.
explanations.D: Affirms one disjunct to deny the other, which is valid but inverts the inferential direction (not the same as eliminating one to conclude the other). The premise affirms rather than eliminates.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent of an implicit conditional rather than eliminating a disjunct: presence of Baroque characteristics does not logically entail the Baroque period without a universal premise. Subtly different in inferential basis.

difficultyReason: The stimulus is a conditional chain using 'unless' (equivalent to 'if not'): unless A, B; B leads to C; not A; therefore C. The 'unless' formulation trips students who translate it incorrectly. Distractors use straightforward 'if…then' chains that seem equivalent but differ in premise structure.
stimulus: Unless a clinical trial includes a control group, its results cannot be considered scientifically valid. The results of this trial cannot be considered scientifically valid if they are to be published in a peer-reviewed journal. This trial does not include a control group. Therefore, its results cannot be published in a peer-reviewed journal.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Unless a contractor is licensed, the work performed cannot be legally certified. Work that cannot be legally certified cannot be included in a public infrastructure bid. This contractor is not licensed. Therefore, this contractor's work cannot be included in a public infrastructure bid.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a clinical trial lacks a control group, it is invalid. All invalid trials are rejected by peer reviewers. This trial lacks a control group. Therefore, this trial will be rejected by peer reviewers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A trial's results are publishable only if its methodology is sound. This trial's methodology is not sound. Therefore, its results are not publishable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either a trial includes a control group or it relies on observational data. This trial does not include a control group. Therefore, it relies on observational data.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unless funding is approved, the research program cannot proceed. The research program has not proceeded. Therefore, funding was not approved.

explanations.correct: The stimulus has the form: unless A → not valid; not valid → not publishable; not A; therefore not publishable. It is a three-premise conditional chain triggered by the 'unless' condition. Choice A mirrors this: unless licensed → not certified; not certified → not in bid; not licensed; therefore not in bid.
explanations.A: Correct. Three-premise conditional chain with 'unless' triggering the first conditional, a second conditional extending the consequence, and a factual premise denying the 'unless' condition. Identical structure.
explanations.B: Uses 'if…lacks' rather than 'unless,' making it a standard modus ponens chain. While logically equivalent in content, the stimulus has three premises including an explicit 'unless' construction; this has the same three steps but lacks the 'unless' framing that defines the structure. More importantly, the conclusion ('rejected') differs in nature from the stimulus's conclusion ('cannot be published').
explanations.C: Only two premises (only if + factual denial = modus tollens). The stimulus has three premises. Premise-count mismatch.
explanations.D: Disjunctive syllogism — completely different logical form from the stimulus's conditional chain.
explanations.E: Three premises but the reasoning is modus tollens applied to the 'unless' (unless funding → cannot proceed; has not proceeded; therefore no funding). The stimulus affirms the 'unless' condition (no control group) and chains forward; this denies the consequent and chains backward.

difficultyReason: The stimulus employs a universal negative (No A are B) combined with a particular premise (x is A) to yield a particular negative conclusion (x is not B). Distractors substitute 'some' for 'no' or invert the subject and predicate of the universal premise, trapping students who scan loosely.
stimulus: No ethical investment fund holds shares in companies that manufacture landmines. The Verdant Growth Fund is an ethical investment fund. Therefore, the Verdant Growth Fund does not hold shares in any company that manufactures landmines.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No peer-reviewed journal publishes articles that lack empirical support. The Annals of Cognitive Science is a peer-reviewed journal. Therefore, the Annals of Cognitive Science does not publish articles lacking empirical support.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some ethical funds avoid fossil fuel stocks. The Verdant Growth Fund is an ethical fund. Therefore, the Verdant Growth Fund may avoid fossil fuel stocks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No fund that holds landmine stocks has been certified as ethical. The Verdant Growth Fund holds no landmine stocks. Therefore, the Verdant Growth Fund can be certified as ethical.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All ethical funds are transparent about their holdings. The Verdant Growth Fund is transparent about its holdings. Therefore, the Verdant Growth Fund is an ethical fund.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No investment fund is both ethical and profitable without compromise. The Verdant Growth Fund is profitable without compromise. Therefore, the Verdant Growth Fund is not ethical.

explanations.correct: The stimulus uses: No A are B (universal negative); x is A; therefore x is not B. Choice A follows the same form: No peer-reviewed journal publishes unsupported articles; Annals is peer-reviewed; therefore Annals does not publish unsupported articles.
explanations.A: Correct. Universal negative ('no peer-reviewed journal…') plus particular affirmative ('Annals is a peer-reviewed journal') yields particular negative conclusion. Identical structure.
explanations.B: Uses 'some' instead of 'no,' making the universal premise a particular affirmative. The conclusion is accordingly weakened to 'may,' creating a strength mismatch with the stimulus's certain conclusion.
explanations.C: Inverts the subject and predicate: the universal premise is 'No fund with landmine stocks is ethical' (no B are A), while the particular premise affirms the predicate (holds no landmine stocks), not the subject. This commits a structural inversion and is actually invalid reasoning (denying the antecedent).
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent: all ethical funds are transparent; Verdant is transparent; therefore Verdant is ethical. This is an invalid inference and differs structurally from the valid universal negative reasoning in the stimulus.
explanations.E: Uses 'no A are both B and C' — a different universal negative form. The particular premise denies one conjunct to conclude the other conjunct is absent. Different structure from the stimulus's simpler no-A-are-B form.

difficultyReason: The stimulus uses a conditional with a necessary condition ('only if') plus modus tollens. One distractor uses 'only if' correctly but commits modus ponens (affirming the antecedent of the derived conditional), which is invalid. Students must carefully distinguish sufficient from necessary conditions.
stimulus: A renewable energy project receives federal subsidies only if it meets the efficiency threshold established by the Energy Department. The solar installation at Pine Ridge did not meet that efficiency threshold. Therefore, the Pine Ridge installation does not receive federal subsidies.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A pharmaceutical drug is approved for sale only if it passes clinical trials administered by a licensed body. The drug Varentix did not pass such clinical trials. Therefore, Varentix is not approved for sale.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A renewable energy project meets the efficiency threshold only if it uses certified components. The Pine Ridge installation uses certified components. Therefore, it meets the efficiency threshold.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a project receives federal subsidies, it must report its energy output annually. The Pine Ridge project does not report its energy output annually. Therefore, it does not receive federal subsidies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All projects that meet the efficiency threshold are eligible for federal subsidies. The Pine Ridge project meets the efficiency threshold. Therefore, the Pine Ridge project is eligible for federal subsidies.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Federal subsidies are granted only to projects approved by the regional board. This project was approved by the regional board. Therefore, this project will receive federal subsidies.

explanations.correct: The stimulus: receives subsidies only if meets threshold → (receives subsidies → meets threshold); did not meet threshold (not Q); therefore does not receive subsidies (not P). This is modus tollens via 'only if.' Choice A: approved only if passes trials → (approved → passes trials); did not pass trials (not Q); therefore not approved (not P). Identical structure.
explanations.A: Correct. 'Only if' creates a necessary condition; denial of that condition via modus tollens yields the conclusion. Premise count, conditional direction, and conclusion strength all match.
explanations.B: Same 'only if' vocabulary but commits the fallacy of affirming the consequent. The 'only if' makes passing clinical trials necessary for approval; meeting the threshold is affirmed; concluding approval follows is invalid. The stimulus is valid; this choice is not.
explanations.C: This is straightforward modus tollens on a sufficient-condition conditional ('if receives subsidies → reports output'; does not report; therefore does not receive). Valid but different structure: the conditional direction differs from the stimulus's 'only if' (where the necessary condition is what is denied).
explanations.D: Universal instantiation (all meeting threshold are eligible; Pine Ridge meets threshold; therefore eligible). Affirms the antecedent of a sufficient-condition universal, not a necessary-condition 'only if.' Different logical form.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent: subsidies only if approved by board (approved → ??? — actually, 'only if approved' means receives subsidies → approved by board); was approved; therefore will receive subsidies. This affirms the consequent and is invalid reasoning.
